elements.element: Vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with a limit of at least USD 1 million per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Section 14.10(a) requires Commerce One to maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with an aggregate limit of at least USD 2 million.
elements.evidence: Section 14.10(a) requires an aggregate commercial general liability limit of not less than $2,000,000.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 2 million.
elements.evidence: Section 14.10(b) requires professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor must maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance of at least USD 5 million.
elements.evidence: Section 14.10(c) requires at least $5,000,000 of cyber and privacy liability insurance where Commerce One processes Corio or Customer data, expressly covering the Customer Data processing condition.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: Section 14.10(d) requires workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor must provide certificates of insurance to Customer upon request.
elements.evidence: The final sentence of Section 14.10 requires Commerce One to provide Corio with certificates evidencing the coverage upon Corio's request.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 1 million.
elements.evidence: Section 14.10(b) requires $2,000,000, which exceeds the fallback $1,000,000 requirement.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor must maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance of at least USD 2 million.
elements.evidence: Section 14.10(c) requires $5,000,000 where Commerce One processes Corio or Customer data, exceeding the conditional fallback limit of $2,000,000.

result.reason: The operative insurance provision satisfies every preferred requirement and therefore also the reduced fallback limits. It is not minimal because it additionally requires all coverage at Commerce One's expense for one year after the agreement ends and expands the cyber trigger to Corio data, none of which is required by either stated position. Unrelated commercial terms remain operative and no substantive contradiction is introduced. Drafting quality is severely impaired because Section 14.11 and the execution preamble appear before the newly added Section 14.10, leaving the provisions misordered and placing operative language after “IN WITNESS WHEREOF.”
